run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:08:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects a small but persistent error signal from frontend-proxy itself: its SERVER spans named "ingress" carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR at roughly 0.5 span/min (0–7.78 spans per 5-minute window), while its CLIENT spans to the frontend backend ("router frontend egress") carry zero errors. At 06:09:01Z the 5-minute error increase was exactly 3.3333 spans, i.e. 0.011111/s, matching the alert annotation value 0.01111111111111111, so the alert is consistent with a >0 threshold on that small error-span rate rather than with a new spike. The proxy's access log shows the concrete failures: HTTP 503 with flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward upstream cluster "frontend", for requests from the load generator (python-requests/2.32.5) on /api/products/*, /api/data, /api/cart and /api/recommendations between 05:43:54Z and 06:11:40Z. The failing hop is therefore frontend-proxy → frontend, but the retained evidence does not show which side closed the connection: frontend has no error spans, no spans over 5s, healthy pod/endpoint state and no restart, while its container produced no log lines at all in the windows checked. No single object is proven as the origin, so no root cause is asserted. The load-generator pod replacement at 05:58:51Z and the flagd loadGeneratorFloodHomepage="on" setting were examined and are not supported as causes.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error signal is on its server spans: the 10-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} went from 0 to between 1.06 and 9.47 spans across 05:39:01–06:17:01Z, while traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="router frontend egress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 0 at every sample.

Over the 60 minutes ending 06:17:52Z the error-span increase was 20.29 spans for frontend-proxy and 0 for frontend, accounting and payment; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each had 3.05–4.06 spans, all on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream client operations.

frontend-proxy's 5-minute error-span increase oscillated between 0 and 7.7778 spans from 05:44:01Z to 06:17:01Z; at 06:09:01Z it was exactly 3.3333 spans per 300 s = 0.011111/s, which equals the alert annotation's current value 0.01111111111111111.

frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 503 responses with response flag UC and response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward upstream cluster "frontend", e.g. GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM at 05:43:54.642Z, GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N and GET /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0 at 05:46:36Z, GET /api/data/?contextKeys=telescopes at 05:48:30Z and GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM at 06:11:40.650Z, all with client "python-requests/2.32.5" and 0 bytes received / 95 bytes sent.
All 21 pods in otel-demo were phase Running with Ready/ContainersReady True, restartCount 0 and empty lastState, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth.
The frontend Service has exactly one endpoint, 100.96.2.93 (pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2, port 8080), and frontend-proxy has exactly one endpoint, 100.96.2.11 (pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth).

No frontend or frontend-proxy spans exceeded 5000 ms in any 10-minute sample (share above 5000 ms = 0), and the share above 1400 ms stayed at 0.02–0.20% for frontend and 0.20–0.46% for frontend-proxy.

Resource use was flat: frontend working set ~242.8–263.6 MB and frontend-proxy ~41.0–41.6 MB across 05:39:01–06:17:01Z; the frontend container (CPU limit 100m, request 50m, memory limit 200Mi, no probes configured) was CPU-throttled in ~25–29% of CFS periods in every 5-minute sample, frontend-proxy in ~4–6%.

The load-generator Deployment rolled its pod at 05:58:51Z: old ReplicaSet load-generator-57ffcd644 (0 replicas, created 05:27:01Z) had pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 deleted at 05:58:52Z and new ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd (created 05:58:51Z) created pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb; both ReplicaSet templates use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator and identical env (LOCUST_USERS=50, LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080).

ConfigMap flagd-config (created 05:27:01Z) has every fault flag adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure at defaultVariant "off"; only loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is "on" (variants off:0/on:100, description "Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests.").

Frontend server-span volume in 06:07:52–06:17:52Z was GET 3012, GET /api/products/{productId} 1671, POST 787, POST /api/cart 587, GET /api/data 333, GET /api/recommendations 299, GET /api/cart 284, POST /api/checkout 200 and GET / only 92.7 spans per 10 minutes, i.e. homepage requests are a minor share of traffic.

load-generator logs between 06:04:56Z and 06:04:59Z show ordinary load-generator activity ("User browsing product: HQTGWGPNH4", "Multi-item checkout completed for user …", "User getting recommendations for product: …").

The named upstream, frontend, shows no failure signal of its own: 0 error spans over the 60 minutes ending 06:17:52Z, 0% of spans above 5000 ms, pod Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and its Service endpoint pointing at that running pod.

There is no crash or eviction mark on the implicated pods: every container in otel-demo reports restartCount 0 with empty lastState, and the only otel-demo events in the window concern the load-generator Deployment/ReplicaSet/pod replacement.

The client-side view of the same traffic does not show errors: frontend-proxy's "router frontend egress" CLIENT spans recorded 0 error spans at every 10-minute sample while its "ingress" SERVER spans carried the errors, so the failure is only visible on the proxy's inbound span.

The 05:58:51Z load-generator pod replacement caused the errors: error spans were already present from 05:44:01Z onward and continued at the same oscillating level (0–7.78 spans per 5 minutes) after the replacement, and the new ReplicaSet reused the same image and identical env.

A crash, OOM kill, eviction or resource exhaustion of frontend or frontend-proxy produced the 503s: no container in otel-demo restarted, restartCount is 0 everywhere, memory use was flat, and no frontend/frontend-proxy span exceeded 5s.

The 503s originate on the frontend-proxy→frontend hop: Envoy returned 503 with upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} toward cluster "frontend", but the evidence cannot say whether Envoy closed a reused keep-alive upstream connection or the frontend process closed it, because the frontend logged nothing and recorded no error span.

The 0.01111111111111111 in the alert is a per-second rate of the same error spans (3.3333 spans / 300 s), consistent with an alert expression rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) > 0, i.e. any error span within 5 minutes fires it; the rule itself could not be read.

The frontend container's low CPU limit (100m) and steady ~25–29% CFS throttling could contribute to intermittent connection handling failures on the proxy's upstream hop, but throttling was at the same level in every observed sample and no latency increase accompanied the errors, so it is not established as the cause.

loadGeneratorFloodHomepage="on" in flagd-config declares frontend homepage flooding; its declared fault does not match the observed traffic path, since GET / is only ~92.7 frontend server spans per 10 minutes against 3012 GET spans and 1671 product-page spans, so it is kept as an unconfirmed candidate rather than the cause.

Read the actual RequestErrorRate rule in the alerting stack (it is not loaded in this Prometheus) and consider requiring an error ratio or a minimum volume / for-duration, because a steady ~0.5 error span/min on a service handling hundreds of ingress requests per minute is enough to keep a >0 threshold firing.

Inspect frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream settings (upstream idle timeout, max requests per connection, retry policy) together with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive/header timeouts to determine which side terminates the upstream connection.

Enable application logging for the frontend pod and re-evaluate the frontend container CPU limit (100m, ~25–29% of CFS periods throttled) if request handling under load is a concern; verify frontend-side behaviour directly instead of inferring it from the proxy.

gaps: The alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with {alertname="RequestErrorRate"} (cd723bbb-7a0e-466f-946e-b3b02f7a51ba-t0:9aac5312-2c1f-4e5f-96e9-5f925bda837c) and with rule_name="RequestErrorRate" (ee34d9f6-c3b3-4d5f-8fde-61d8e258117d-t0:985a7d68-6b00-4a5d-9871-f4c9bfed4e57) both returned no data, so the rule expression, threshold and evaluation window are unverified; the 0.0111 value is only numerically consistent with a 5-minute error-span rate.

Frontend application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 in 05:39–05:50Z (bbc3dcb2-8195-4dcc-966c-ef5e8e1a0dbb-t1:87bc9515-2ee6-4812-be4a-5b41b9f6607a), 05:50–06:17Z (7f23c52d-af1f-4001-a9e1-c9acc8c7a2b4-t1:2e24ecee-4bd3-41a5-9025-efb540df01a1) and 06:10–06:17Z (651f032b-96d7-4d6a-ad22-ad51e2bb9bf5-t1:87d8532b-119b-45f6-a38f-93f450ae18c3) returned zero log lines (no_data), so frontend-side runtime errors cannot be read and the frontend cannot be fully cleared or blamed.

Jaeger holds no traces for the error window: traces_search for frontend-proxy (f5742d0a-d958-410c-bd95-35554336a679-t0:f54c73e5-b224-4a7b-96eb-c3a1fa61fc5d) and frontend (cc7ed92c-009a-4863-a26f-dbb4a3eee218-t0:ab92ae93-3d74-47d0-93dd-0fa848f35936) returned nothing for 05:50–06:17Z, the error-tag search returned nothing (cd723bbb-7a0e-466f-946e-b3b02f7a51ba-t1:af4c637d-a9dd-43b3-bae4-8540d50067ce), and the kept frontend-proxy result ended at ~05:41:19Z (aa1f81a6-96cf-4b97-9787-b096b8d1f33a-t1:a9b23329-8c15-4e25-b13f-93acb9abcab4, RESULT_TOO_LARGE, not citable), so no error trace and no span parent references were available to confirm the frontend-proxy→frontend call edge or inspect error details.

No pre-incident baseline exists: span-metric samples begin ~05:39–05:44Z inside the policy window, so it cannot be determined whether the ~0.5 error span/min and the ~25–29% frontend CPU throttling are new or chronic, nor when the error rate first deviated.

ConfigMap flagd-config carries only a creationTimestamp (05:27:01Z) and no last-updated marker, so whether loadGeneratorFloodHomepage or any other flag value was changed during the incident window is unknown; flagd pod logs returned no matching lines (fc9cc0f4-7ada-4e13-b62f-a9f7edd98321-t0:cd5ae56d-e542-4936-8081-8b92be0e5155).

A NetworkPolicies query in otel-demo returned an empty list (efe3351a-76e3-4d2c-8b15-c6313d2b7b02-t2:09d140cc-8560-4241-8ab8-29f7d5396fd7, nothing matched), a query for http_*/rpc_*/kube_deployment series returned nothing (cc7ed92c-009a-4863-a26f-dbb4a3eee218-t2:81360788-3f41-4829-9534-b213cc8b84ca, cd723bbb-7a0e-466f-946e-b3b02f7a51ba-t2:a54f751c-743a-46ac-8ecd-8987b0857ad6, f5742d0a-d958-410c-bd95-35554336a679-t1:4a9f3f0d-53a9-4512-ad3c-40cb273f4a6c), and one query form failed (cdfa359d-8707-4bf0-8911-5e96228148bf-t0:7c428b84-1cea-4c5b-914b-feb9373ac04e, no_data with le="5000" string), so network-policy refusal and kube-state-metrics-based object state could not be assessed.

Change history is not integrated in this Run (change_history not_integrated), so no deployment/config change record exists to explain when or how the condition started; unrelated Events in the data-recorders namespace (Job/PVC/StatefulSet activity) were not tied to otel-demo and were left out of the conclusion.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the Alertmanager/Prometheus stack that produced the alert and confirm its expression, threshold and for-duration.

Inspect frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration and Envoy admin stats (upstream_cx_destroy, upstream_rq_5xx, upstream_reset metrics) for the frontend cluster, and compare keep-alive/upstream idle timeouts against the frontend HTTP server settings.

Enable or fix frontend application logging and sample the frontend process directly (its access/error logs and connection handling) during a reproduction of the 503/UC upstream_reset_before_response_started pattern.

Review whether the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage flag being "on" and the 50-user Locust load match the intended demo load, and record change history for flagd-config and workload specs so future windows have a baseline.
